text.p: - Only one of four ministerial candidates proposed by prime minister-designate Janez Drnovsek passed a parliamentary board hearing on Thursday. However Drnovsek will not have to name any new candidates as a vote on the candidates will be taken in the parliament.
- Slovenia will spend 45 million tolars ($302,000) in the first half of this year to restore forests damaged by heavy snow and ice this winter.
- Electricity prices will increase by 4.9 percent on Saturday. The government said the increase would contribute 0.22 percent to the annual inflation rate.
- The number of throat cancer victims in Slovenia is increasing rapidly and is already well above the European average, cancer experts warned.
- A survey by daily Dnevnik showed that 60 percent of Slovenians support the government proposed by prime Janez Drnovsek and 32.5 percent said they were against it.
- Firemen rescued around 800 children from a fire in a Ljubljana school on Thursday morning. There were no casualties. Experts are investigating the cause of the fire.
- The number of visits to casinos owned by the company Hit rose five percent in 1996 to 1,850,000.
- Slovenian exports in the first 11 months of 1996 fell five percent compared to the same period a year ago, economists said.
